Most people with depression point to current world happenings, the uncaring and marginalizing institutions, or the focus on money over wellbeing as a source of depression. Are they wrong?

I think this is somewhat correct.

You could say cancer is a purely genetic ailment if you remove environment as well.

Plenty of studies show that things like stress and nutrition activate or suppress genes which can either help, hinder, or even fight cancer.
So when discussing disease there is often a tension between nature and nurture.

Well, sure, rationalization is a powerful thing. Many years ago, researchers connected electrodes to the motor centers of the brain, and when they'd push a particular button to make the subject raise his arm, they'd ask him why his arm went up. He'd invariably reply "Because I wanted to raise it."
There probably is some philosophical point to be gleaned from this.
It's worth reading up on anosognosia to think clearly about how relevant this is.
